title: Design System: OSAS Scholarship Allocation System

display.purpose: The unauthenticated front door only. Never inside the application.

figure.purpose: One per region: the number the region exists to report, always inside a sentence or title block that says what it counts.

lead.purpose: The page h1 and every section heading, at one weight.

body.purpose: All running copy, table cells, inputs, buttons, rail items, box titles (at 600).

annot.purpose: Archivo Narrow, uppercase, tracked: column headers, field labels, title-block and box-cell keys, status marks. Never a sentence.

mono.purpose: Values a reader must transcribe exactly: student numbers, reference numbers, literal CSV headers.

shadows.name: seat
shadows.purpose: Sheets, boxes, inputs, primary buttons. Edge definition only.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Modals, over a Seal Green scrim at 55%.

shadows.name: focus-ring-gold
shadows.purpose: Focus on any Seal Green surface: 2px Gold at 2px offset, offset colour taken from the surface behind.

shadows.name: focus-ring-seal
shadows.purpose: Focus on any Linen or white control, and the global focus-visible floor.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Every hover, focus and colour change, including a box border warming to Seal Green.

motion.name: ease-sheet
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for overlay entrances at 200-300ms; exits run faster than entrances.

narrative.overview:
A scholarship is a surveyed parcel. It has a bounded capacity you can count, a closing date in its title block, and lots that are either awarded or open. A student's application is a **claim staked on one lot** — on record, in a known position, against a capacity that is drawn rather than described.

That mapping is exact, not decorative. Slots are lots. The deadline is a closing date. The pass list is the recorded survey that settles every lot at once. "3 of 10 slots filled" stops being a sentence a worried student has to parse and becomes three hatched lots out of ten they can count in a glance, on a phone, in sunlight.

The surface is the drafting table that plan is drawn on. The shell — the navigation rail and the page's header band — is a committed field of **Seal Green**, a deep drafting ink. The working sheets laid on it are **Linen**, a warm off-white, because a plan is printed on stock and because pure white glares on a cheap Android screen outdoors. Structure is carried by **line weight and hatch density**, the way a drawing carries it: hairlines, witness marks, tick rails, and 45° hatching. Depth is not the medium here; measurement is.

Density is administrative and unapologetic — tight uppercase annotation in Archivo Narrow against generous drawing space — but body copy runs at **15px, not 14**, because the reader is often an anxious nineteen-year-old on mobile data who needs to read a decision, not skim a queue.

The system raises its voice exactly twice. **Citation Gold** appears only on a record that belongs to the person reading it. **Oxide** appears only on a refusal or a destructive control. Everything else is Seal Green, Seal Green, Grant green, or a neutral.
keyCharacteristics: A Seal Green shell framing Linen sheets; no grey screen with one accent
Capacity drawn as countable lots, never estimated as a bar or a ring
Four interior type sizes; rank carried by weight, case, reversal and rule
Two voices — Archivo for reading, Archivo Narrow for annotation — plus a mono reserved to values you must transcribe
True corners on the plan geometry, 2px on the controls you touch
Citation Gold means *yours*; Grant green means *settled*; Oxide means *refused*
The student's Dashboard and Scholarships page are two panes of same-anatomy boxes; every other screen keeps sheets as containers, not scaffold

rules.name: The Committed Shell Rule
rules.body: The rail and strip are a Seal Green field. If a new shell element needs separation it takes a Seal Line hairline or a step to Seal Deep — never a grey.

rules.name: The Never-Grey-On-Colour Rule
rules.body: Secondary text on any coloured surface is tinted from that surface's own hue, never from the neutral ramp. Seal Tint exists precisely because the previous system set Slate on its coloured rail and landed at 4.39:1 — a real, measured failure.

rules.name: The Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold marks ownership and waiting, and nothing else. It is never a general accent and never a large fill. **On paper it is never text** (1.5:1 on Linen); there it appears only as a focus ring on green, as a wash behind a pending mark carrying Ink, and in the seal. On the Seal Deep front door it *is* legible as text at 7.1:1, and is used there for the university's name — the one place gold sets type.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: Green and gold are the only hues. Grant and Oxide are semantic states, not palette colours, and they appear only inside a mark, a wash, or a destructive control. If something new wants a colour and it is neither the university's nor a state, it is a neutral.

rules.name: The Countable Capacity Rule
rules.body: Quantities with a unit a reader cares about — slots, documents, days — are drawn as discrete countable marks or set as aligned figures. Never a progress bar, ring, donut, or sparkline. A reader must never estimate a length to learn a number they could have counted.

rules.name: The Product's Words Rule
rules.body: The world lends type, palette, density and the parcel. It never lends vocabulary. On screen a scholarship has **slots**, a student sends an **application**, and OSAS settles them with a **pass list** — the office's own words, which PRODUCT.md and the controller rules both use. "Parcel", "lot" and "claim" name the drawing in code, in CSS classes and in this document; they never appear in an interface string. A metaphor that starts renaming the product's nouns has stopped being a design and become a costume.

rules.name: The Readable Ink Rule
rules.body: On paper, only Ink, Graphite and Slate carry text. On the shell, only white and Seal Tint. Every colour-only or glyph-only signal pairs with an sr-only word carrying the same meaning.

rules.name: The Four Sizes Rule
rules.body: The authenticated application has exactly four type sizes, published as tokens. No component may introduce a fifth, and no component may reach for `display`. When something needs to feel more important, it changes weight, case, or reversal, or it gains a rule above it — it does not get bigger. The previous system drifted to a welcome line at 18px sitting above its own section headings at 16px; a fixed scale makes that impossible.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with tracking belongs to Archivo Narrow at Annot size, and only ever to the labels around data: table column headers, title-block keys, status marks. It never touches a sentence, a heading, a button, or a paragraph of statute.

rules.name: The One Figure Rule
rules.body: A region reports one number at Figure size. If two numbers compete, one of them is Body — rank them, or the reader ranks them wrongly. This is also what keeps the system off the hero-metric template: a Figure always sits inside a sentence or a title block that says what it counts, never in a tile of its own.

rules.name: The Transcription Rule
rules.body: Spline Sans Mono is for values a reader must copy exactly: student numbers, application reference numbers, literal CSV headers. Wanting to look technical is not a reason to reach for it.

rules.name: The Tabular Default
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on `html`, so every figure in the product aligns without a component having to remember. The previous system made this a rule and then lost it on exactly the columns it warned about.

rules.name: The Task-Container Rule
rules.body: Pick the container from what the reader is doing, not from how much content there is. 1280px means "compare columns". 1024px means "read down a list". 672px means "read a record or a sentence".

rules.name: The Rail-Only Rule
rules.body: Wayfinding lives in the rail. The narrow-screen strip is a disclosure control plus a page label; it must never grow links, a search field, or an account menu.

rules.name: The Named Page Rule
rules.body: Every authenticated screen sets a page title, and the narrow strip prints the current page's name. The previous system shipped a `$header` slot no view ever filled and a single `<title>` for the whole application, which left every page announcing itself identically.

rules.name: The Two Panes Rule
rules.body: The student Dashboard and Scholarships page are the one approved place where a grid of same-size boxes is the page's structure. It holds only there and only under three limits: every box in a grid sets the same facts in the same cells, so two can be compared at a glance; a box never nests inside a box; and the boxes carry the student's own record and the scholarships open to them, nothing ornamental. Admin surfaces are unchanged and keep sheets as containers, not scaffold.

rules.name: The True Corner Rule
rules.body: If it is part of the drawing, it is square. If it is a control, it is 2px. There is no third radius, and nothing in the authenticated application is fully round except the seal.

rules.name: The No Costume Rule
rules.body: The world lends type, palette, density, and the parcel. It does not lend the navigation model or the controls. Every control is the standard one a visitor already knows — real buttons, tabs, inputs, selects, tables with sortable headers — never a drafting instrument's bezel, a drawn ruler standing in for a slider, or ruled paper standing in for a table.

rules.name: The Two-Ring Rule
rules.body: A focus ring is 2px at 2px offset, and its hue comes from the surface it sits on: **Gold** on any Seal Green surface — the primary button, the rail items, the strip trigger — which is the signature pairing and reads at 4.0:1 against the green; **Seal Green** on any Linen or white control; and the control own hue on a semantically coloured control. The ring offset colour is the surface behind it, so a ring never sits on a mismatched halo. A global focus-visible floor in app.css guarantees nothing is ever left wearing the browser default outline — which the previous system left on its mobile wordmark.

rules.name: The One Clause Rule
rules.body: On the student panes, copy states the count or the reason in one short clause and stops. It never explains the rules behind it: "You can apply to 1 more scholarship.", not a paragraph on the limit before the limit is shown.

dos: **Do** make the shell a Seal Green field, and tint any secondary text on it from Seal Green rather than greying it.
**Do** draw a capacity as countable lots and write the same number beside them.
**Do** mark the reader's own record in Gold, and nothing else in Gold.
**Do** keep to four interior type sizes, and change weight, case or rule when something needs rank.
**Do** put uppercase tracking only on Archivo Narrow annotation around data.
**Do** give every region exactly one Figure, inside a sentence or a title block that says what it counts.
**Do** set a page title on every screen and print the page's name in the narrow strip.
**Do** write a real empty state for every list, and never render a heading above an empty container.
**Do** state the elapsed wait on a pending record. The office can already see it; the student is the one who needs it.
**Do** print a record's reference number wherever that record is shown, in Spline Sans Mono.
**Do** pair every colour-only or glyph-only signal with `sr-only` words.
**Do** build the student Dashboard and Scholarships page as two panes of same-anatomy boxes, each setting the same facts in the same Annot-over-Body cells.
**Do** state a count or a reason on the student panes in one short clause.
**Do** keep state transitions at 150ms, overlay entrances at 200–300ms with an exponential ease-out, and exits faster than entrances.
donts: **Don't** reintroduce a neutral shell with one accent colour. That is the look this system replaced.
**Don't** set grey text on any coloured surface. Tint it from the surface's hue.
**Don't** use Gold as a text colour, a brand accent, or a large fill.
**Don't** put Seal Green on a destructive, dismissive or cancelling control. Destructive is Oxide and nothing else.
**Don't** represent a quantity as a progress bar, ring, donut, or sparkline.
**Don't** add a fifth interior type size, and don't use `display` inside the application.
**Don't** put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading. The heading carries its own weight. A title block goes beneath.

**Don't** build a grid of same-size sheets as a page's structure, and never nest a sheet in a sheet. The student Dashboard and Scholarships page are the one approved exception, under the Two Panes Rule; the no-nesting half holds there too.
**Don't** explain the rules on a student surface before or instead of showing the count. One clause, then the drawing.
**Don't** uppercase a button label or shrink a secondary button's type.
**Don't** round the plan geometry, and don't introduce a third radius.
**Don't** dress a standard control as a drafting instrument. The world lends type, palette, density and the parcel — never the controls or the navigation model.
**Don't** collapse a data table into stacked cards on mobile; scroll it inside `overflow-x-auto`.
**Don't** use a glyph or emoji in place of an icon. Icons are authored SVG at one consistent stroke.

**Don't** use `diffForHumans()` for a deadline. It phrases futures as "1 day from now" and truncates fractional days, so a date two days out reads as one. Count whole calendar days between day boundaries.
**Don't** show a deadline alone on a scholarship that is full, closed or ended. State the binding reason first; a bare deadline reads as open.
